title: Kinase inhibitor under-prediction diagnosis (prospective N=5 batch)
question: Why does Sisyphus under-predict 4/5 kinase inhibitors by 2-6x in the new prospective batch?

vorasidenib.hypothesis: Very low absolute bioavailability (F=27% reported by FDA) not captured by engine; engine assumes high absorption from peff=2.40

pirtobrutinib.hypothesis: Unusually low actual clearance (CL/F=2.05 L/h, very slow). VDss predicted 100L vs reported 32L (3x over-predicted)

pacritinib.hypothesis: ML particularly bad (14x off). High accumulation ratio (AR=3.86) implies long effective t1/2 not captured

crinecerfont.hypothesis: EXTREME_LIPOPHILIC (logP=6.42) OOD for ML. Engine nearly 2-fold (best of batch). ML collapses to low value.

revumenib.hypothesis: Engine within 2-fold (1.6x). Mild case. VDss 5.0 L/kg predicted; actual likely lower.

F1_engine_beats_meta_on_batch.finding: Engine-only would be 19% better than Meta on this batch. ML drags Meta down.

F2_drugs_are_right_tail_outliers.finding: 3/5 drugs are at 67-81st percentile of kinase class (higher Cmax per dose than typical). ML predicts toward class mean, missing the tail.

F3_ML_trained_kinases_are_fine.finding: ML is NOT broken on kinase inhibitors generally. It's broken on these specific drugs which are tail cases.

F4_VDss_overpredicted_for_some.finding: VDss over-prediction contributes to Cmax under-prediction (more drug distributed → lower peak)

dominant_failure_modes: Mode 1 (UNDER-prediction): ML Cmax model regresses toward training mean for OOD drugs with unusually low clearance. VDss may also be over-predicted for some.
Mode 2 (OVER-prediction): Engine assumes high absorption (peff-driven) for drugs with actual low bioavailability (F<30%)
actionable_next_steps: SHORT-TERM: Add AR-based uncertainty flag for prospective validation (drugs with known AR>3 have noisier reference values)
SHORT-TERM: Honest reporting — N=15 prospective AAFE 2.48 ≈ holdout 2.74 (no free lunch)
MEDIUM: VDss model retraining with kinase-inhibitor-enriched dataset (VDss data from DrugBank)
MEDIUM: Absolute bioavailability (F) predictor for engine calibration (peff → F correction)
LONG: Class-aware meta-learner (MW>450 + logP 3-5 → engine-weighted blend for kinase class)
conclusion: The prospective AAFE 2.48 is an HONEST performance metric. The under-prediction is not due to a single fixable bug but to the known CLint R²=0.24 ceiling + distribution shift for tail cases. The original N=10 AAFE 1.68 claim overstated Sisyphus's generalization.
